q: Alcohols may be considered as derivatives of alkanes where one hydrogen atom is replaced by a _____ group.
e: Alcohols may be considered as derivatives of alkanes where one hydrogen atom is replaced by a hydroxyl group. An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2.

q: Most of the common reactions of all alcohols are due to the functional group, _____.
e: Most of the common reactions of all alcohols are due to the functional group, -OH. An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon. A functional group is the atom or group that sets the characteristic reactions of an organic molecule.

q: Alcohols form a homologous series with the general formula _____.
e: Alcohols form a homologous series with the general formula C_nH2n+1OH. An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon. A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same functional group and a general formula that rises by CH2. A general formula such as CnH2n+2 describes a whole homologous series at once.

q: In the IUPAC system, the chain of an alcohol is numbered from the end nearest the _____ group.
e: In the IUPAC system, the chain of an alcohol is numbered from the end nearest the -OH group. An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon.

q: Alcohols containing at least _____ carbon atoms have more than one structure and form isomers.
e: Alcohols containing at least three carbon atoms have more than one structure and form isomers. An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon. Isomers share a molecular formula but differ in how the atoms are arranged, so their properties differ.

q: Ethene and steam are passed over a _____ catalyst at 570°C and 60-70 atmospheric pressure to produce ethanol.
e: Ethene and steam are passed over a phosphoric acid catalyst at 570°C and 60-70 atmospheric pressure to produce ethanol. A catalyst speeds a reaction by lowering activation energy and is not used up in the overall change.

q: In the fermentation method, starch is treated with freshly germinated barley called malt, which contains the enzyme _____.
e: In the fermentation method, starch is treated with freshly germinated barley called malt, which contains the enzyme diastase. Fermentation uses yeast without air to turn glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

q: The enzyme _____ converts maltose into glucose during fermentation.
e: The enzyme maltase converts maltose into glucose during fermentation. Fermentation uses yeast without air to turn glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

q: The enzyme _____ converts glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide during fermentation.
e: The enzyme zymase converts glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide during fermentation. Fermentation uses yeast without air to turn glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

q: The fermented product contains about 11% ethanol and is fractionally distilled to yield rectified spirit containing about _____% ethanol.
e: The fermented product contains about 11% ethanol and is fractionally distilled to yield rectified spirit containing about 95% ethanol. The fermented product contains about 11% ethanol and.

q: Alcohols from methanol to butanol are mobile liquids, while those above $C_{11}OH$ are usually _____.
e: Alcohols from methanol to butanol are mobile liquids, while those above C11OH are usually solids. An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon.

q: The first two members of the alcohol family, methanol and ethanol, are miscible with water in any _____.
e: The first two members of the alcohol family, methanol and ethanol, are miscible with water in any proportion. An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon.

q: The most toxic member of the alcohol family is _____.
e: The most toxic member of the alcohol family is methanol. An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon.

q: When a piece of sodium is added to ethanol, reaction occurs at room temperature, liberating _____ gas.
e: When a piece of sodium is added to ethanol, reaction occurs at room temperature, liberating hydrogen gas. Listen for hydrogen in that sentence.

q: When ethanol is heated with an excess of concentrated sulphuric acid at 160°C, _____ is produced.
e: When ethanol is heated with an excess of concentrated sulphuric acid at 160°C, ethene is produced. Concentrated sulphuric acid is viscous, dehydrating and oxidising as well as strongly acidic. Concentrated sulphuric acid is a strong acid, a dehydrating agent and an oxidising agent.

q: When ethanol is heated with a smaller proportion of concentrated sulphuric acid at 140°C, _____ is formed.
e: When ethanol is heated with a smaller proportion of concentrated sulphuric acid at 140°C, diethyl ether is formed. Concentrated sulphuric acid is viscous, dehydrating and oxidising as well as strongly acidic. Concentrated sulphuric acid is a strong acid, a dehydrating agent and an oxidising agent.

q: The reaction of an alcohol with an acid to produce an ester and water is called _____.
e: The reaction of an alcohol with an acid to produce an ester and water is called esterification. An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon. An ester forms when a carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol, and it is the functional group in many flavours and fats.

q: Ethyl ethanoate is an ester that has a pleasant _____ odour.
e: Ethyl ethanoate is an ester that has a pleasant fruity odour. An ester forms when a carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol, and it is the functional group in many flavours and fats.

q: When ethanol vapour is passed over freshly reduced copper heated at 300°C, removal of hydrogen occurs with the formation of _____.
e: When ethanol vapour is passed over freshly reduced copper heated at 300°C, removal of hydrogen occurs with the formation of ethanal. Listen for ethanal in that sentence.

q: When ethanol is heated with acidified potassium dichromate solution, oxidation takes place in two stages to finally give _____.
e: When ethanol is heated with acidified potassium dichromate solution, oxidation takes place in two stages to finally give ethanoic acid. Oxidation takes place in two stages to finally give ethanoic acid. Ethanoic acid is the word this version is asking about.
